$comment: What the stats monitor watches. It NEVER edits site data — it only alerts (via a GitHub issue) when a public source drifts from these baselines, so a human can verify in-app and update. When you confirm and update a real figure on the site, bump its baseline here too.

metrics.label: Spotify monthly listeners
metrics.note: Current monthly listeners. Verified 28 Aug 2026 on Spotify's own artist page (55,701,680, #49 in the world), which agreed with kworb exactly. Monitor-only — no siteTargets — because the site publishes the all-time PEAK (spotify-peak-listeners), not the current figure. Do not conflate the two: the peak is 60.13M and cannot fall. CROSS-CHECKED 4 Sep 2026: kworb read 52,813,789, a 5.2% FALL, and the same figure Spotify's own page showed that day (recorded in app/data/africasBiggest.ts). That correctly trips this metric — relativeDrift is absolute, so a fall alerts exactly like a rise — and the weekly issue for it is the alarm working, not a stale config. The baseline is deliberately NOT bumped to the kworb reading: it records the last value read at the PRIMARY source by a human, and overwriting that with an automated pull would both downgrade its provenance and silence the alert someone is meant to act on. Bump it when you next read Spotify's own page. Worth a thought while you are here: a current-listeners figure swings far more than 3% across a release cycle, so this threshold will keep firing on ordinary decline — raise it if the weekly issue stops being read.

metrics.label: Spotify peak monthly listeners (all-time high)

The bot overwrote Tyla's peak with his on every run from 31 Jul (46.58M -> 58.77M -> 58.99M -> 59.21M) while the figure it was meant to update never moved off 58.48M.

His best in the log is No. 36, so that label was wrong at any rank above it; it now describes where he currently sits.
metrics.$comment: sanity.maxJump was 10, but withinSanity reads maxJump as a FRACTION of the baseline — |live-46|/46 > 10 needs live > 506, and max:500 already rejected that, so the jump guard was unreachable and the rank published unguarded. It is now maxDelta: 10, an absolute bound of ten chart places, which is what the 10 meant.

metrics.label: Total Spotify streams (all songs)
metrics.note: RE-ANCHORED 10 Sep 2026 to ChartMasters, by Paul's decision. offset = the SAME-DATE gap between ChartMasters and kworb on the 9 Sep reading: 10,956,307,905 - 10,844,002,099 = 112,305,806. Both sides of that subtraction are dated reads of the same day; see docs/sourcing/CAREER-STREAMS-OFFSET.md. WHAT IS AND IS NOT EVIDENCED. 80,606,612 of the 112,305,806 was measured track by track on 10 Sep - 42 credited recordings that exist on Spotify but are absent from kworb's 291-row roster, each read at open.spotify.com/track/<id> and joined by track id, every one of them on another artist's release or a various-artists compilation, which is what the artist-page 'appears on' shelf kworb reads simply drops. The remaining 31,699,194 is NOT separately attributed: it is the amount by which ChartMasters' roster exceeds both kworb's and our own catalogue hunt. The mechanism is named and plausible - catalogue completeness, the same mechanism, counted further - but it has not been enumerated. Do not describe the whole 112,305,806 as measured. TWO CLAIMS THE PREVIOUS NOTE MADE THAT ARE FALSE AT THE BODY, recorded so they are not reinstated: kworb does NOT 'undercount featured credits' - its total already contains 4,640,678,029 of them, 43% of the figure - and the gap does not GROW. IT DECAYS, AND THAT IS THE MAINTENANCE JOB. kworb's cumulative has been rising about 10.81M/day against actual streaming near 7.6M/day, which is a tracker absorbing catalogue it previously missed; every unit of that closes this gap. So this offset will drift the published figure ABOVE ChartMasters over time. Re-read ChartMasters and re-subtract against kworb's raw on the SAME date whenever the two are compared, and never do arithmetic on the published figure to derive it. The bot cannot self-correct this: 31M on 10.9B is 0.3%, far under the metric's 3% threshold.
metrics.$comment: Cumulative and therefore monotonic: kind is "peak" so a dip in the source can never be published as a fall in an all-time total. It was "drift" until 25 Aug 2026, which let 10.80B be rewritten to 10.78B.

metrics.label: Tems — 2026 Spotify streams (running total)
metrics.note: Year-to-date Spotify streams, kept as a LEDGER: a checkpoint (the total through a date) plus each later day's streams under the date kworb's page is stamped with. Published = checkpoint + every daily to the group's common day — the newest day all five ledgers cover without a hole — and the checkpoint rolls forward on each write; all five rows or none; a hold on any member holds all. Never the change in kworb's cumulative total (kworb absorbs catalogue it had not tracked: Tems' total rose 138M between 27 Aug and 9 Sep 2026 while her days summed to 74M), and never dailies keyed by the bot's run date (that added Burna Boy's 27 Aug, 29 Aug and 2 Sep twice and never added 28 Aug, 31 Aug or 9 Sep; net small — the board's false Burna-over-Wizkid reading of 11 Sep was several small things adding up, see docs/sourcing/STREAMS-2026-ANCHOR.md). No relative jump guard: dailyMax gates each day on the way in, and after a hold a week's worth is a legitimate move. ANCHOR: the fan tracker @WITTIEWIZ's '2026 so far' post of 10 Sep 2026 11:31 UTC (x.com/WITTIEWIZ/status/2098011367378735458), through kworb's pages stamped 2026/09/09 (Tems: through her 09/08 page — kworb published no 09/09 page for her, and neither the tracker nor this ledger has that day). Summed once per kworb day, kworb's own dailies and the tracker's count agree within a few million over the fortnight before. Re-anchor from the tracker's next 'so far' post whenever the two drift by more than a day's streams, and whenever a gap is reported. The baseline is always the checkpoint's value; re-anchoring means moving both together. JOINT PLACES: a row less than tieWithin (10M — about a day's streams at each end of the window) below the row above is written `tie: true` and the board shows them level; the mark comes off the day the gap opens past it. Paul's decision, 12 Sep 2026, option (b) in the doc. THIS ARTIST: 09/10 daily is the exact figure on her page (stamped 09/10 on 12 Sep). SKIPPED STAMPS: when kworb's next page for this artist skips a day, the skipped day's streams are derived from the page's own totals (fillSkippedDays), gated to 0.5–1.5× the two stamped dailies around it, and listed as derived in the run summary; a gap that fails the gate is left as a hole for a hand.
